images.note: Real screenshot from Apache Airflow's own official documentation ('UI Overview' page), showing the DAG Overview's Grid tab: a run-by-run, task-by-task grid of colored status bars across a DAG's execution history, with the task list down the left side.

Real screenshot from Apache Airflow's own official documentation, showing an actual task instance's Logs tab: real log output for one task run, including timestamps and the task's stdout, exactly what a student clicks into when a task needs investigating.

imageNote: Both images found via curl against airflow.apache.org's raw HTML (confirmed not JS-rendered — image paths are present as plain relative hrefs resolved against the page's own directory, per this catalog's Ch1 finding). Checked ch01/01-why-orchestration/sources.json first to avoid reusing an image: that lesson used dag_overview_dashboard.png (the DAG-level Overview tab with failure counters), which is a different screen from both images used here (the Grid tab's run history, and one task instance's actual log output) — no overlap. These two screens are the direct answer to 'where do you actually look when monitoring a production deployment': the Grid gives the at-a-glance run history, the Logs tab gives the actual text output when something needs a closer look.
